summary: This is a JUnit test class for a Thermostat. The first test checks that a chilly room in normal mode reports "Heating"; the second checks that eco mode tolerates a cooler room, so 66 degrees stays "Idle" instead of firing the heat.

lines.text: Brings in the @Test annotation from JUnit 5, which is what marks a method as a test the runner should execute.
A static import lets you call assertEquals directly instead of writing Assertions.assertEquals every time.
Tests live in their own class, named after the class under test with "Test" appended — a convention that makes test files easy to find.
Tells JUnit that the method beneath it is a test case to run and report on independently.
The method name states the expected behaviour in plain words, so a failure message tells you what broke without reading the body.
Builds the object under test with eco mode off: this is the "arrange" step, setting up exactly the situation the test cares about.
Compares the expected value (first argument) against the actual result; if they differ, JUnit fails the test and shows both values.
The second test covers the new eco-mode behaviour, kept separate from the first so each failure points at one rule.
Passing true for eco mode with a temperature of 66 sits between the two thresholds, which is the only region where eco mode changes the answer.
Asserts that eco mode leaves the heat off at 66 degrees, proving the lower threshold is actually being applied.
